A laboratory setup showing a round-bottom flask containing a mixture of ammonium chloride and sodium nitrite solutions, heated with a Bunsen burner. A delivery tube leads from the flask to a pneumatic trough, where nitrogen gas bubbles up into an inverted gas jar filled with water. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A flowchart of the Haber Process. On the left, inputs "Nitrogen gas (N₂)" and "Hydrogen gas (H₂)" enter a compressor. The compressed gases move into a reactor tank. A pipe leads from the reactor to a cooling condenser, where liquid ammonia drips into a collection tank. Unreacted N₂ and H₂ are shown recycling back to the reactor.

A test tube held at a slight angle. The bottom half contains dense, clear concentrated H₂SO₄. The top half contains a paler aqueous solution. Exactly at the boundary between the two liquids, a distinct dark brown ring is visible.

Two side-by-side molecular models. Left: Diamond, showing carbon atoms connected in a rigid, rigid 3D tetrahedral lattice. Right: Graphite, showing carbon atoms arranged in flat sheets of hexagons, with dashed lines indicating weak forces between the distinct separated layers.
